overview.heading: How the Text to Image Generator works
paragraphs: You write a description, choose Nano Banana or GPT Image, and pick a shape, a resolution and, with GPT Image, a transparent background or an animated GIF. PiCraft sends your words to the model you chose, exactly as you typed them, and gives you back the file the model made. There is no style menu, no template and no crop, so what you write is what the model sees, and what the model returns is what you download.

That makes the description the whole job. If you want a watercolor, say watercolor. If you want a photo taken at golden hour, say that. The models read the same sentence a little differently, which is why the model switch is there: run an idea on two of them, keep the better image, and use that result to work out what to change next.

Every image is a new roll of the dice, so a second or third try of the same idea is normal. Each image uses credits (1 for 1K, 2 for 2K, 3 for 4K, and 2 or 3 for an animated GIF), and the credits come back automatically when an image can't be made. A good habit is to explore at 1K and spend the larger resolutions on the version you are going to use.

whatYouGet.title: The original file
whatYouGet.description: You download the image as the model returned it, at the pixel size that belongs to the shape and resolution you chose. Nothing is cropped, recolored or compressed on our side.

whatYouGet.title: A smaller JPG copy
whatYouGet.description: Next to the original comes a JPG copy that is lighter to send, post or attach. Use the original when you need every pixel and the JPG when you need a small file.

whatYouGet.title: Your choice of model
whatYouGet.description: Nano Banana, GPT Image 2.6 and GPT Image 2.5 are listed side by side on the form. Switch between them for the same description and compare the results yourself.

whatYouGet.title: Shapes from square to panorama
whatYouGet.description: Pick a shape that fits where the image is going, from 1:1 to 21:9, and with GPT Image banners such as 2:1 and 3:1. Nano Banana adds tall strips like 1:4 and wide strips like 4:1, and both make 4:5 portraits.

whatYouGet.title: A transparent background
whatYouGet.description: Choose Transparent with GPT Image and the PNG comes with no background, so a sticker, an icon or a product can go straight onto a page, a shirt mockup or a sticker sheet. A JPG copy on white comes with it.

whatYouGet.title: An animated GIF
whatYouGet.description: Choose Animated GIF with GPT Image 2.6, pick 6, 9 or 12 frames and a speed, and download a looping GIF. It costs 2 or 3 credits.

whatYouGet.title: Up to 4K
whatYouGet.description: Choose 1K, 2K or 4K: Nano Banana goes up to 4K and GPT Image up to 2K. PiCraft shows only the resolutions each model supports for the shape you picked, with the price next to each one.

whatYouGet.title: A record of your images
whatYouGet.description: Finished images are listed under My files in the same browser for 90 days, so you can come back and download them again.

useCases.title: Blog headers and slides
useCases.description: Describe the scene your post is about and pick 16:9. You get a header that fits the post instead of a stock photo that almost does.

useCases.title: Pinterest and social posts
useCases.description: Make an original vertical image for a board or a post. 2:3 is the Pinterest shape, and 9:16 fills a phone screen for Stories and short video covers.

useCases.title: Wallpapers and prints
useCases.description: Imagine a place, a pattern or a creature and use it as a phone wallpaper, a desktop background or a poster. 4K gives you room to print or crop.

useCases.title: Concept art and storyboards
useCases.description: Try a character, a room or a mood before you commit to it. Panoramic shapes such as 21:9 are good for establishing shots.

useCases.title: Product and packaging ideas
useCases.description: Mock up how a product might look on a counter, on a shelf or in a scene, then take the idea to a photographer or to the specific makers for a spec-ready file.

useCases.title: Stickers, icons and overlays
useCases.description: Ask for one subject, choose Transparent and you get a PNG with the background already removed, ready for a sticker sheet, a presentation or a design file.

useCases.title: Reaction GIFs and animated avatars
useCases.description: Describe a character and what it does, such as a fox that waves and then blinks, and make a looping GIF for a chat, a newsletter or a profile.

useCases.title: Banners and page headers
useCases.description: GPT Image makes wide 2:1 and 3:1 shapes, and Nano Banana goes to 4:1 and 8:1, so a header or a divider can have the shape of the place it goes.

tips.title: Start with the subject, then the place
tips.description: "A red fox reading a book in an armchair by a rainy window" says who, what and where in one line. Everything else you add should change the picture in a way you can name.

tips.title: Say the look in plain words
tips.description: Write the medium and the finish you want: watercolor, oil painting, flat vector illustration, 3D render, photograph with a shallow depth of field. There is no style menu to do it for you.

tips.title: Name the light
tips.description: Soft window light, golden hour, neon at night, overcast noon. Light changes the mood more than any other single word.

tips.title: Put exact words in quotes
tips.description: If the image needs text, such as a poster title, write it in quotes and keep it short. Read every letter of the result before you use it.

tips.title: Pick the shape before you write
tips.description: A tall subject such as a lighthouse suits 9:16, and a desert suits 21:9. Choosing the shape first helps you describe a picture that fits it.

tips.title: Change one thing at a time
tips.description: If the result misses, adjust one detail and create it again. That shows you what each word does and saves credits.

tips.title: Explore small, finish large
tips.description: Try ideas at 1K, then create the final version at 2K or 4K. Remember that a larger file is a new image, not an enlargement of the first.

tips.title: For a transparent background, ask for one subject
tips.description: Describe a single subject on its own, such as "a sticker of a coffee cup, flat illustration, white outline". Soft shadows and glows can leave a faint edge, so look at the result on a light and a dark background before you use it.

tips.title: For a GIF, describe the motion in order
tips.description: Say what moves and in what order: "a fox waves, then blinks, then waves again". A simple, repeating motion works better than a story. Fewer frames give a bigger picture; more frames give a longer loop.

styleGuide.heading: Nano Banana or GPT Image?
styleGuide.intro: These models all turn a description into an image, and none of them is better at everything. These are the practical differences on PiCraft. For anything else, try your own description on each.

items.title: Nano Banana 2.1, by Google
items.description: Makes 14 shapes plus Auto, including 4:5, 5:4 and the strips 1:4, 4:1, 1:8 and 8:1, and offers 4K for every shape. It also takes up to 10 reference images in the Image to Image Generator.

items.title: GPT Image 2.6 and 2.5, by OpenAI
items.description: Both make 14 shapes plus Auto, including 4:5, 5:4 and the wide 2:1 and 3:1, at 1K and 2K (Auto at 1K only). Both can leave the background transparent and take up to 16 reference images in the Image to Image Generator. Only GPT Image 2.6 makes animated GIFs.

items.title: The price
items.description: The same for every model at the same resolution: 1 credit at 1K, 2 at 2K and 3 at 4K (GPT Image goes up to 2K). A transparent background costs the same as an image, and an animated GIF costs 2 credits for 6 frames and 3 for 9 or 12.

items.title: How long each takes
items.description: Measured on PiCraft in November 2026, at 1K: Nano Banana 2.1 took 10 to 34 seconds over 27 images, about 18 on average. GPT Image 2.5 took 13 to 56 seconds over 11 images, and 10 of them finished in under 30 seconds. In our own tests GPT Image 2.6 took about 20 to 40 seconds at 1K and 2K, with a transparent background and for GIFs. We do not have enough 4K runs to give a figure, so expect those to take longer. Times change with load. The earlier runs were mostly edits from reference images.

items.title: When the result matters
items.description: Create the same description with each model and keep the better one. Results vary from image to image, so one try is not a verdict on a model.

checklist.heading: Before you download
items: Check the subject: is everything you named in the picture, and nothing odd that you did not ask for?
Look closely at hands, faces and small objects, which is where AI mistakes show first.
Read every letter of any text that was drawn into the image.
Confirm that the shape and the pixel size shown next to the download match the place the image will go.
If the image looks realistic, check the platform's rules on labeling AI-generated content before you post it.
Download the files now. Generated files are deleted after 90 days.

limits: The result is never exactly the same twice. If you need the same character or scene again, use the Image to Image Generator with the earlier result as a reference.
Text in images is the most common thing to go wrong. Short, quoted words work best, and every letter needs a check.
Every model applies its own safety checks and can refuse a request. When that happens no image is made and the credits are returned.
The pixel size is set by the model. If a place needs an exact size, such as a 1280×720 thumbnail, use the matching maker, which crops and exports to that spec.
Realistic images of real, identifiable people, other people's characters and brand logos can infringe rights or mislead viewers. You are responsible for what you describe and publish.

A GIF is a short loop drawn on one sheet, not a video. The frames are small (about 960 px square for 6 frames, 820 px for 12), the motion is simple, and the subject can change slightly from frame to frame.
A transparent background comes from GPT Image only, and GIFs from GPT Image 2.6 only. Nano Banana and GPT Image 2.5 do not make GIFs.
PiCraft makes PNG, JPG and GIF files. It does not make SVG or other vector files.
